criteria.description: A data structure is a specialized way of organizing, storing, and managing data in computer memory so that it can be accessed, processed, and updated efficiently.
Classification into linear (elements arranged sequentially/adjacently) and non-linear data structures (hierarchical or network relationships).
Correctly identify examples of linear and non-linear data structures.
An algorithm is a finite set of well-defined, step-by-step instructions designed to solve a problem or perform a computation.
List and describe key characteristics of a good algorithm.
Complexity analysis evaluates the efficiency of an algorithm with respect to input size by determining how time and memory requirements grow.
Time complexity measures the execution time or number of operations required by an algorithm relative to input size.
Space complexity measures the amount of memory or storage required by an algorithm during execution.
Mention of best, average, and worst case analysis for evaluating performance under different conditions.
An array is a linear data structure storing elements of the same data type in contiguous memory locations with fixed size and fast index-based access.
A linked list is a linear data structure of nodes storing data and pointers/references to the next node in non-contiguous memory, supporting dynamic sizing and efficient insertion/deletion.
